ground_truth.note: String-literal reference, not an attribute access: a static delta over resolved symbols is expected to MISS it; found only by the runtime failure.

ground_truth.breaks: `{{ 'www.example.org' | urlize }}` links to http://www.example.org on 2.11 and https://www.example.org on 3.1; same call, no error, no warning
ground_truth.source: Jinja2 3.1.0 changelog: urlize adds https:// to bare www links by default

notes: Cross-package same-object successor test: in the old env `jinja2.Markup is markupsafe.Markup` and `jinja2.escape is markupsafe.escape` are both True (checked with `is`), so a delta engine that follows an object to the module it now lives in should offer markupsafe.Markup / markupsafe.escape, and the migrated app (which must add `import markupsafe`) renders byte-identical output on 3.1. MarkupSafe moves 1.1.1 -> 3.0.2 in the same migration (Jinja2 3.1 needs MarkupSafe>=2.0). Old Jinja2 2.11.3 emits NO warnings for any of these (verified with -W error on py3.9), so the baseline offers no runtime warning to predict from (S4). Environment(autoescape=...) defaults did not change (False in both; the app sets autoescape explicitly), so there is no DEFAULT entry. `jinja2.ext.with_` is a string-literal reference (see its entry). The change scenario's `urlize` happens inside the template, so the observable boundary symbol is Template.render (the recorded call), not the filter. Manual migration adds `import markupsafe` right after `import jinja2`; if pymolt's rewrites already added it, the duplicate import is harmless. Equivalence checked: original app on py3.9/2.11.3 and migrated app on py3.12/3.1.6 print identical repr() for render_page (escaped and unescaped), render_string, render_row, safe_label; pytest 5/5 on both, 6/6 in the change scenario on both.
